title: Notvorrat: visuelle Welt wählen
question: The roll assigned the Aicher-style pictogram programme. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Erscheinungsbild Haushalt
options.lineage: Otl Aicher's Munich '72 identity programme and its pictogram system
options.thesis: The household supply as an identity programme: every food group gets a grid-built pictogram and a programme colour, with calm cheerfulness instead of the red-and-black of alarm.
options.viewport: A wall of eight food-group fields in programme colours, each with its pictogram, the Soll line and the Ist fill, plus one large 'Tage versorgt' figure and the next MHD due.
options.risk: Can become a Munich '72 costume, or a generic tile grid if the grid and pictograms aren't strictly built.

raised.raise: Length is exact time: each batch's MHD bar has a length equal to its remaining days on one shared time scale, so nothing in the timeline is decorative.
Numbers at true density: every quantity is set in tabular figures in aligned columns, with no rounding into vague 'almost full'.
A fixed-capacity frame: Soll is a ruled container that visibly fills; overstock is a stated state, not a silent overflow.
A strict state vocabulary for every batch: frisch · bald fällig · fällig · abgelaufen, always as words plus pictogram, never colour alone.

options.label: Lagerkarte (Kardex)
options.lineage: German office stock-card files: Bestandskarte, Zugang/Abgang/Bestand, coloured rider tabs
options.thesis: Every item is a stock card in a sliding file: Zugang/Abgang/Bestand columns, and coloured rider tabs along the top edge mark the month each batch expires.
options.viewport: A visible card file: overlapping card edges, item names on the visible strip, riders lined up by expiry month so the next due batches stand out.
options.risk: Close to the most obvious 'inventory' metaphor, and paper-office nostalgia could read dusty.

options.label: Gridded specimen
options.thesis: The supply drawn on a visible construction grid: cells are units (person-days), and stock literally fills grid cells.
options.viewport: A huge cell-built 'Tage' figure over a grid where each cell is one person-day of supply, filled or open.
options.case: Holds product clarity (cells as person-days is honest), but the audience doesn't recognise it as theirs.
options.risk: Becomes a type poster that obscures the shopping list.

options.label: Labanotation score
options.lineage: dance notation: block length is exact duration
options.thesis: Batches as shaped blocks on a vertical staff where the future sits above.
options.viewport: A vertical time staff of MHD blocks.
options.case: Fuses poorly: nobody in the household reads a dance score.
options.risk: Opaque to anyone who is not a notator.
options.kept: Length is exact time: MHD bars are drawn to scale.

options.label: Datamatics field
options.thesis: Stock as a strobing barcode field.
options.case: Loses on both axes: cold and hostile for a calm household tool.
options.risk: Alarmist and unreadable on a phone.

options.label: Mixtape J-card
options.lineage: hand-lettered cassette inlays timed to fill a side
options.thesis: Shelves as tape sides that must fill exactly.
options.case: Fuses weakly: the nostalgia has nothing to do with provisions.

options.label: Lexicon page
options.lineage: 19th-century lexicon with guide words and colour plates
options.thesis: The inventory as a lexicon with guide words.
options.viewport: A dense text column of items.
options.case: Loses on both axes for a phone-in-pantry task.
options.kept: Rank by apparatus, not size (folded into batch detail).

options.label: Transit diagram
options.thesis: Food groups as metro lines, MHD dates as stations.
options.case: Forced mapping: a pantry has no journeys.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean inventory dashboard: sidebar, KPI cards, progress bars, and traffic-light expiry badges.
canonCard.viewport: KPI row (Tage versorgt, Artikel, bald fällig), then category progress bars and an expiry table.
